title: What Time It Is at Boot: A Clock That Starts in 1970, the Jump When It Is Set, and Records That Sort Themselves Wrongly

questions.question: Which clock should every timeout and rate of the robot be measured in?
options: Time since boot, which only goes forward and cannot be set
questions.explanation: A wall clock timeout fires at the sync.

questions.question: The clock is set at 40 s on a boot that started in 1970. How big is the jump?
options: About 1.79e9 s, 56.9 years, in one step while 0.2 s of real time passed
questions.explanation: classify calls it a step forward.

questions.question: A timeout of 0.3 s is measured on the wall clock, and the clock is put back an hour. When does it fire?
options: Never: the elapsed time is negative

questions.question: Sorted by the wall clock, how many of six records of two boots were in the wrong place?
options: 5: the early records of the second boot carry 1970 time and go before the whole of the first boot
questions.explanation: By boot and time since boot, none.

questions.question: Why does check_validity answer unknown before the clock is set?
options: A 1970 clock says not yet valid for a certificate that is fine: a guess must not be used to say yes or no
questions.explanation: The robot needs the time without a certificate.

questions.question: What does a robot that suspends do to the monotonic clock on many systems?
options: It does not count the suspended time, so time since boot is shorter than the real time
